opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nathaniel Young (employee ID E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E031.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nathaniel Young (E031) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, write is permitted, and the requested level is within policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E031 is a contractor with basic security training (note conflicting with HR's claim of full-time). Contractors with basic training max out at read; write is not permitted. Recommend read for Payroll.
reason: Nathaniel Young (E031) requests write access to Payroll. There is conflicting employment information: HR lists E031 as full-time Payroll Specialist (which would allow write), while the Security agent reports from the Security DB that E031 is a contractor with only basic security training. Under policy, contractors with basic training are capped at read and never admin. Given the unresolved conflict, I apply the stricter applicable limit and grant read, matching the Security agent's recommendation.
